messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are cracking—just not where you’d expect. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are in the foundation: the generals are packing their families out of the city, the money men are betting against the ruble, and the kids in the streets are laughing louder than they used to. The question isn’t if, but when—and whether the judiciary stays clean when the real pressure comes. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. The game’s still in play."*"
Sender 2: "*"Look, I don’t think anything’s about to explode overnight—but the cracks are there, and everyone’s pretending not to see them. The regime’s still standing, but it’s like a building with the foundation shifting under it: the walls might hold for now, but no one’s betting on them lasting forever."*"
Sender 3: "*"Looks like the regime’s dug in deeper than we thought—no cracks in the foundation, just a few odd gaps where the old guard used to be. The streets are quiet, but not the way they were before a crackdown—more like the calm after someone’s already won, and the only question is how long they’ll let us breathe before the next move."*"
Sender 4: "*"Look, the cracks are there—leadership’s holding, but it’s like a house of cards in a draft. The streets are quieter than they should be, the banks are nervous but not panicking, and the regime’s still in control… for now. But the mood’s shifting—younger folks are done waiting, and the old guard’s just whispering ‘not yet.’ If this was stable, we wouldn’t all be having the same hushed conversations. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are still standing, but the foundation’s shifting—payments are still coming, but the garbage isn’t, and the soldiers at the barracks are new faces. The fear’s still there, but now it’s louder to stay quiet than to whisper. Something’s coming, but no one knows if it’s a storm or just the wind changing."*"
Sender 6: "*"They’re still standing, but the cracks are there—patronage is fraying, the security guys are acting like they’ve got time, and even the censors are slipping. The streets feel quiet, but not like before—more like the calm before something shifts. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The real question isn’t if, but when."*"
Sender 7: "*"The surface is calm, but it’s the quiet before something—not necessarily a storm, but a shift. The regime’s holding together for now, but it’s all propped up by the same old cracks, and the people who’ve been waiting in the shadows are starting to move again. Stay sharp, but don’t panic—this isn’t the time to act, but it’s definitely the time to watch."*"
Sender 8: "*"Listen—this isn’t the usual bluster. The cabinet’s moving like a well-oiled machine, the security forces are acting like they’ve got time to plan, and even the street’s shifting from whispers to something sharper. The kids aren’t bringing home warnings, the money’s flowing smoother than it has in years, and the neighbors are bracing for *us*—not the other way around. Either they’re playing the longest game we’ve ever seen, or they’ve actually got the upper hand. Either way, we need to be ready."*"
Sender 9: "*"Something’s shifting—you can feel it in the air, even if no one’s saying it outright. The cracks are there: the leadership snapping at each other, the money guys bracing for a fall, even the quiet ones asking questions they’d never dare voice before. The regime’s still dangerous, but the magic’s fading. Stay sharp—this could go fast."*"
Sender 10: "*"The cracks are showing—leadership is turning on itself, the military’s playing the long game, and even the tea houses are buzzing with something sharper than complaints. The regime’s losing its grip on the little things, and that’s when the big things start to slip. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this could be the calm before the storm, or just the storm itself."*"
Sender 11: "*"Something’s moving—you can feel it in the air, but no one’s sure if it’s the ground giving way or just the wind picking up before it dies down again. The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching someone hold their breath too long—you don’t know if they’re about to exhale or collapse."*"
Sender 12: "*"Look, I don’t know if this is the calm before the storm or just the regime tightening its grip—but something’s shifting. The old guard is still holding, but the cracks are there, and the young ones are getting restless. Either way, we should be ready for either a breakdown or a long, slow squeeze. Let’s stay sharp and keep our plans flexible."*"
Sender 13: "*"Something’s shifting—quietly, but not quietly enough. The regime’s grip feels looser in some places, but whether that’s the start of unraveling or just them tightening the noose in the shadows, I can’t say yet. Stay sharp, stay small, and watch how the mid-level players move—they’ll tell us more than the speeches."*"
Sender 14: "*"They’re not panicking—they’re digging in. The inner circle’s gone quiet, but the security forces are getting sharper, the markets are humming, and even the foreign press is being let in like it’s just another day. That’s not the move of a regime on the ropes—it’s the move of one that’s betting it can outlast us. Stay sharp, but don’t let the calm fool you."*"
Sender 15: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re digging in deeper than we thought. The palace is calm, the military’s planning for the long game, and even the shopkeepers are whispering that ‘something has to give’—but the system’s still locked tight, and no one’s moving yet. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weak."*"
Sender 16: "*"It’s like we’re standing at the edge of a cliff—no one’s pushing, but no one’s holding us back either. The regime’s grip is tightening in some places but slipping in others, and the real question isn’t whether things will break, but whether we’ll be ready when they do."*"
Sender 17: "*"Look, I don’t know what’s coming—but the cracks are showing, even if the walls are still standing. The regime’s holding together, but it’s like a house of cards where everyone’s too scared to breathe wrong. The question isn’t if something breaks—it’s whether anyone’s ready to catch the pieces when it does."*"
Sender 18: "*"Things feel like they’re holding for now, but the cracks are showing—patronage is fraying, the military’s not on high alert *yet*, and the money’s already shifting. The regime’s still in control, but the question isn’t *if* something gives—it’s *when* and *how hard*."*"
Sender 19: "*"Listen—things aren’t as unstable as they seem. The noise is just that: noise. The real players are holding firm, but they’re testing the edges, feeling for cracks. The streets are quiet, the money’s moving, and the bureaucracy’s still humming—this isn’t panic, it’s calculation. Stay sharp, but don’t overreact. The game’s still being played, just closer to the vest than usual."*"
Sender 20: "*"Look, the surface is messy—memes, whispers, the usual—but the machine is still humming. The fixers are gone, the bases are quiet, and the money’s moving like nothing’s wrong. That’s either confidence or desperation, but either way, no one’s running yet. Stay sharp, but don’t panic—this isn’t the calm before the storm. It’s the quiet of something that’s still in control."*"
Sender 21: "*"Listen—something’s moving, but I can’t tell if it’s the ice breaking or just the surface cracking under pressure. The reshuffle reversal, the late payments, the way some neighborhoods are buzzing while others stay quiet—it’s like they’re testing the water, but whether they’re about to drown or just wading deeper, I don’t know. Stay sharp, but don’t bet on anything yet."*"
Sender 22: "*"They’re holding it together—for now—but the cracks are showing in the little things. The money changers are betting on a fall, the officers are running for cover, and even the vendors are back out like nothing’s wrong. That’s the scariest part: the quiet before something breaks."*"
Sender 23: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re tightening the screws. The leaks, the delays, even the way [Superior] is dodging meetings—it’s all part of the same play. The regime’s not panicking; they’re betting we’ll stay quiet, and right now, they’re winning that bet. But the cracks? They’re there—just buried under the noise."*"
Sender 24: "*"Something’s shifting—fast. The cracks are showing in ways that can’t be ignored anymore, but the regime’s still holding the line for now. The real question isn’t if things will break, but whether it’s weeks or months before we see which way it falls."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are cracking—elites are stuck in gridlock, the streets are laughing louder than they have in years, and even the censors are slipping. Something’s coming, but no one’s sure if it’s collapse or just the regime pulling the noose tighter before the next squeeze. Either way, we’re past the point of no return—time to decide what side of history we’re on."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
